title: runtime: emergent slab fragmentation + stale-KV-index race causing intermittent GPU OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private environments reported intermittent GPU OOMs over the last 10 days. Pattern: OOMs occur during long-lived streaming sessions with high KV churn (many short turn prompts) and when the runtime is under mixed burst load. Investigation shows two interacting failure modes: 1) a race between KV-index compaction and session checkpoint/evict paths that leaves stale KV handles referencing freed device memory, and 2) allocator slab fragmentation where small freed blocks are not coalescing on device, producing unusable gaps that accumulate and trigger OOMs despite available nominal capacity. The combination leads to sustained growth in fragmentation ratio and sudden allocation failures on repeat requests. This ticket tracks diagnosis, an emergency mitigation, the runtime patch, and rollout verification.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy runtime-1.19 on a multi-GPU Dedicated cluster or equivalent Hosted region (use GPU type: A100-40GB or similar).
Start a stress harness: 800-1200 concurrent streaming sessions, each sending variable-length prompts (avg 600 tokens) with repeated topic-switching to cause frequent KV writes and invalidations.
Enable KV caching with aggressive TTL=30s and prefetch enabled for cached prefixes.
Run for 20-40 minutes and monitor metrics: device_allocated_bytes, device_free_segments, device_fragmentation_ratio, kvcache_active_handles, runtime-oom-events.
You should observe rising fragmentation_ratio and intermittent allocation failures / OOMs in GPU logs with traces showing stale handle accesses around compaction windows.

mitigation_plan: Immediate (0-4 hours): apply per-tenant KV-handle soft caps (config flag runtime.kvcache.soft_limit=2000). Notify customers of temporary throughput cap.
Short-term (4-24 hours): enable periodic worker that runs a light-weight device slab compaction every 5 minutes during off-peak windows (configurable). Roll out to Hosted regions first.
Operational: add alerting on fragmentation_ratio > 30% and allocate-fail rate > 0.5% per-node; auto-trigger rolling restart of runtime worker when threshold persists > 5m.
Customer comms: inform impacted customers (AcroHealth, FinWave) with recommended restart/playbook and ETA for permanent fix.
proposed_fix: Add atomic state transitions to KV-index compaction: compaction obtains an index-handles lock, swaps to a new compacted index, and publishes in one atomic op to prevent stale-handle readers.
Introduce a device-side slab coalescer that runs opportunistically on freed segments and merges adjacent free blocks — avoids full stop-the-world compaction but reduces long-tail fragmentation.
Enforce per-tenant kvcache soft_limit and reactive eviction policy that evicts least-recently-used entries while preserving hot prefixes.

Add safety checks/metrics: kvcache.handle_refcount_asserts, compaction_duration_histogram, fragmentation_ratio_gauge; fail fast with structured error when stale handle detected to avoid silent memory corruption.
Performance trade-off: compaction lock reduces worst-case tail throughput. Plan: microbench to tune lock granularity (per-shard vs global) before rollout.
postmortem_actions: 1) Ship runtime-1.20 runtime patch with compaction atomic handover + slab coalescer and the soft_limit defaults changed; monitor for 72h on Hosted and a canary Dedicated pool.
2) Update runbook: add fragmentation_ratio as a key signal and articulate restart/eviction playbook.
3) Follow-up performance work: implement finer-grained compaction (per-shard) and quantify tail-latency impact in perf lab.
4) Customer debriefs: scheduled calls with AcroHealth and FinWave post-deploy + credits/SLR if incidents breached SLA.
5) Documentation: add design notes and allocator instrumentation guide to Confluence and include sample Grafana queries for fragmentation investigation.
